problem_statement: Write a program to remove all duplicate values from a list using a loop, maintaining the original order of elements. Given Input: [1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5]. Expected Output: Unique List: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.description: This dimension evaluates whether the algorithm's logic accurately identifies and removes duplicate values while preserving the original order of unique elements for all valid inputs.
sub_criteria: The algorithm correctly identifies an element as unique if it has not been encountered before in the resulting unique list.
The algorithm adds an element to the result list only if it is genuinely a new unique value.
The algorithm ensures the final list maintains the relative order of elements as they first appeared in the original input list.

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.description: This dimension assesses if all necessary structural components of the algorithm are present, including proper initialization, iteration, and handling of various input scenarios.
sub_criteria: An empty list or similar data structure is initialized to store the unique elements.
A loop structure is used to iterate through all elements of the input list.
A mechanism is present to check if an element already exists within the list of unique elements compiled so far.
The algorithm correctly handles edge cases, such as an empty input list or a list containing only unique elements.

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.description: This dimension evaluates the readability and human-understandability of the pseudocode, ensuring the logical steps and variable references are clear and easy to follow.
sub_criteria: The purpose of each major step (e.g., initializing the unique list, iterating through the input, checking for uniqueness) is clear and understandable.
Any variables or temporary storage used are clearly named, and their roles within the algorithm are unambiguous.
The overall flow of the algorithm is logical and easy to trace from start to finish, without confusing jumps or unclear conditions.

dimensions.name: Efficiency
dimensions.description: This dimension examines if the algorithm avoids obviously unnecessary computations or redundant operations, reflecting an understanding of basic performance considerations for list processing.
sub_criteria: The algorithm processes each element of the input list in a single pass or sequence of operations without unnecessary re-scans of the entire input list.

The method for identifying unique elements avoids redundant comparisons or repeated computations for the same element that would significantly increase processing time beyond a common introductory approach.
